Well, OK. I have no information about that so I'll have to take your
word. But it's kind of beside the point. The point I'm making is if
there were really any kind of real popular sentiment at all that DU or
KR needed banning or fixing, it's seems like we should have seen
something on this newsgroup at some point. Now I would be the first
to admit I miss things that go on here because I really skip a lot of
stuff I see. So if anyone knows of a thread or something(s) I missed
out on, please feel free to educate me. But I do tend to watch the
subject names of the threads that go on for any length of time and
my perception is that there's really been nothing. And if so, that's my
issue with it.

We've had huge debates on the newsgroup about Protect Thine Own. There's
clearly a certain segment on the newsgroup that feel Anarch Revolt needs
addressing, however much I disagree. There's a few other things people
will talk about from time to time, like the issue Orpheus and a few others
have with the withdrawl rule.

Don't get me wrong, I don't and have never believed anything ought to be
put up to a popular vote to see what should be banned or changed. I
think ultimately White Wolf just decides what's in their interests to
change and I think they have pretty good incentive to do well by the
players. I just think that if you're going to pick up an issue that
the players themselves haven't been complaining about (or haven't been
complaining about *much* clearly) and make a change, you leave yourself
open to the charge that these things are decided by the elite few who
dismiss the sentiment of the 'unwashed masses' and do what they want.
And the claim that "discsions are nearly continuous, here, in email,
on forums, on chats, face to face, etc." rings hollow. Apparently, they
must have been some of those other places because far from going on
"nearly continuous(ly)" *HERE*, by contrast my perception is that such
discussions didn't go on here at all.

Don't know where, if anywhere, I'm going with this. I guess I just
wanted to explore why I feel sympathy for the people who feel this
was just sprung on them. Other changes from time to time seem to come
out of nowhere (sudden card changes, like the 'Camille, the Raven' thing)
though this is probably the most visible situation in which I've ever
noticed it happen. I don't understand why this happens and I feel it's
sort of a bad sign.

> Most the people I associated with understood that it was stupidly powerful, and game defining by its presence.

Oh, I certainly did, too. And some of the better players I run into
who's skill I respect. But I suspect there are other cards that fall
into that category as well. And, in any case, I don't see how that
status alone makes it a good candidate for outright, sudden banning
when noone seemed to be asking for such a move.

Fred

So maybe it's a waste of time figuring out new versions of these cards

to suggest new text for these, they should be radically changed.

Maybe the seat-switching effect should be temporary, just to allow a
vote deck some turns to breathe, with restrictions to what it could do
to his "temporary" prey?

That would make seat-switching very similar to what Gambit Accepted and
Life Boon do to VP distribution - and a very defensive strategy, which
I suspect doesn't address all of LSJ's concerns; it seems that he
considers using DU and KR as a means to "escape" dangerous predators as
disruptive as using it for vp-snipping. But it makes for interesting
situations. It could not allow a vote deck to take advantage of, say,
Anarch Revolt. The vote deck could buy some time to recover from a
fierce rush deck as predator, but it still should need to prepare and
cope with it later *and* would have to prevent the target of the
switching from dying.

Or this could be a bad idea at all. I don't know. In fact, sometimes
I'm struck with how difficult it is to deal with CCG design. So call me
a yes-man, I don't care - let's play the game as it is and I'm fine
with any change, mmmmm'kay?

are annoyed enough to go start threads about how it should be banned.
Then _maybe_ you start thinking about it.

> We have designers, they design.

Well, let's get something straight: taking cards away != designing new
cards. When you design new cards, the whole process is speculative.
You need to be as careful as you can but let's face it, you have to put
stuff out so the company can sell it. Besides, when it's out, people
don't have to buy it. But banning isn't the same as "designing". I mean
it is design on some level, I agree, but you're doing something different.
People own those cards, they've bought the expansion they were printed
in, they've traded for them and so forth. Plus, the designers are working
from known information, so there's no excuse for banning something that
doesn't *positively* need to be banned. That is, there's no reason to
be as tolerant of mistakes in this process as there is for creating new
cards.

broad base of players aren't being listened to. Be honest about it: say,

How about:

Dramatic Upheaval
Type: Political Action
Political Card - Worth 1 Vote. Called by any vampire at +1 stealth.

Choose another Methuselah. Successful referendum means you switch

places with that Methuselah. *Any Methuselah may discard their hand to
cause this referendum to fail. Only one Dramatic Upheaval may be
played each turn.*

And similar for Kindred Restructure.

This maintains the threat of table switching, but in effect, I think,
it will almost always result in the player it most influences
discarding their hand - destroying their current plans (maybe) but not
their position. That is, it will most often disrupt a player that is
about to take an oust - not a bad thing - and not change the
predator/prey relationship.

Every player has a hand (even if there are no cards in it) so no player
needs to play any differently because of the existence of the cards.

It may marginally increase the value of Storage Annex, I suppose, and
ash-heap retrival cards (mostly, Necromancy). It (may) help Slaughter
House based decks too - at least it could be synergistic with
Brinksmanship.

It also produces a card cycling vote that has much the same effect as
Deal with the Devil (as the controller of the acting minion will be the
first able to discard their hand). Neither good nor bad, just a
comment.

I think that this proposal will mean that DU/KR no longer (effectively)
break the predator/prey relationship and will also not totally
wallpaper them.

seating position.

his hand to prevent you from taking his VP.

getting away - unless you put someone even weaker in front of him, in

That's the whole point though. To provide a dis-incentive to stop people
from switching wrecklessly or from stealing other people's kills.

> The proposed change doesn't allow for the semi-universally "acceptable"
> use that others are attempting to posit, which is that the card can be
> used to get away from a "bad" seating position -- because part of the

But if you allow for a switching effect that focuses on protecting your own
seating, by default it still leaves open the quandary of how to reward your
old predator and your new predator for their previous efforts after you've
moved. It's not something that's easily quantifiable because you can't rely
on the speed, efficiency or equivalence of each other deck on the table.

In any case, as other people have noted here (and elsewhere) other deck
strategies currently have no way of switching places, and in that sense
voting decks always had an unfair advantage in that they could do something
that nobody else could. Removing that ability is a step towards balance, not
away from it. (There is a seperate argument for giving other decks access to
equivalent abilities instead taking it away, which I'd personally perhaps
prefer to see, but that's a whole 'nother ball park).

apply to switching table positions. You pays your money and you takes your
chances. I have seen Gambit Accepted used well, and I have seen it used
badly. TBH I think it's yet to be assimilated fully into the meta-game, and
when it is, we'll see it a bit more. Most players here are still playing
catch-up from Anarchs and Black Hand, let alone Gehenna... *shrugs*

*very* different from web forums. This is not a "better" or "worse"

their own reasons. I'd rather not have Usenet become an extended web
board because people using it have no idea that it's even slightly
different.

like some of the interface changes, for example.
